panel.title: RoomMind
panel.subtitle: Climate management
panel.no_areas: No areas configured in Home Assistant.
panel.no_areas_hint: Add areas in HA settings to get started.
badge.beta_hint: This feature is in beta and may change or be restructured in future updates.
room.control_mode.full_control_info: RoomMind has full control over your climate devices. An external temperature sensor provides the actual room temperature, enabling proportional setpoint calculation. The device setpoint is dynamically adjusted based on MPC power output. The thermal model (EKF) learns your room's behavior for optimal comfort and energy efficiency.
room.control_mode.managed_info: RoomMind sets the target temperature on your device (from schedule, override, or vacation settings), but the device self-regulates using its own internal sensor. No proportional boost, no thermal model learning, and no MPC optimization. For more precise control, assign an external temperature sensor in the Devices section.
room.climate_control_hint: When disabled, RoomMind stops controlling devices in this room. They keep their current settings and may continue heating or cooling on their own. RoomMind will not turn them off.
room.outdoor_hint: Disables climate control, mold detection, and model training. Sensor monitoring continues.
override.label: Temporary Override
override.invalid_band: Cooling target must be at or above the heating target
hero.mpc_learning_paused.outdoor_unavail: RoomMind needs an outdoor temperature to learn this room's thermal model. The configured outdoor sensor is unavailable and no weather entity is set as a fallback. Configure either in Settings.
hero.compressor_protection_min_off_left: Compressor protection: waiting for min-off, {minutes} min left
hero.compressor_protection_info: This room shares an outdoor compressor with other rooms. To prevent short-cycling, the shared compressor group enforces a minimum run time and a minimum off time before this device is allowed to switch again.
hero.coil_dry_info: The AC is running its evaporator drying cycle and switches off afterwards. Cooling demand cancels it immediately.
mode.auto_desc: Heats & cools automatically based on target temperature
mode.heat_only_desc: Heats only. With thermostats in the room, ACs stay off unless smart source selection is on
mode.cool_only_desc: Only uses ACs, thermostats stay off
schedule.create_helper_hint: Create new schedule helper in HA settings
schedule.selector_warning: Multiple schedules but no selector set. Only the first will be used.
schedule.no_schedules: None configured - the room runs on its fixed Comfort and Eco targets until you add one. Tariffs are not day-planning: a change time exists only once your source has published one. For a scheduled tariff (calendars, windows, next change), a base schedule is the right structure.
schedule.preheat_hint: Starts heating early so the room is warm when a warmer schedule block begins (also when a vacation or override ends). Turn off for rooms that should not heat up beforehand, e.g. a bedroom at night: heating then starts only shortly before the block.
schedule.help_temps_title: How is the target temperature determined?
schedule.help_temps: The target temperature follows this priority chain:
schedule.help_temps_1: Manual override – A temporary boost/eco/custom override always takes highest priority.
schedule.help_temps_2: Block temperature – If the active schedule block has a temperature value in its data, that value is used.
schedule.help_temps_3: Comfort temperature – If the schedule is "on" but the block has no temperature, the comfort fallback temperature below is used.
schedule.help_temps_4: Eco temperature – When the schedule is "off" (outside all time blocks), the eco temperature is used.
schedule.help_block: You can set a specific temperature for each time block by adding a temperature value in the schedule's YAML configuration:
schedule.help_block_note: If a block has no temperature data, the comfort fallback temperature is used instead.
schedule.help_split: For auto-mode rooms, you can set separate heating and cooling targets per time block using heat_temperature and cool_temperature:
schedule.help_split_note: If only one is set, the other falls back to the room's comfort temperature. These keys take priority over temperature when present.
schedule.help_multi: You can add multiple schedules and switch between them using a selector entity. This can be an input_boolean (toggles between schedule 1 and 2) or an input_number (selects by number). Without a selector entity, only the first schedule is used.
schedule.comfort_hint_auto: Comfort: target when schedule is on. Eco: target when schedule is off. Rows set the target for heating and cooling.
schedule.comfort_hint: Used when schedule is "on" but no temperature is set in the block
schedule.block_temp_rejected: Values outside the valid range {min}–{max}{unit}: {values}. The comfort target is used instead — check the schedule helper for a typo.
schedule.bases_hint: Shared time-of-day schedules for the house or a floor. Bind the ones this room should follow; when a block here and a room block cover the same hour, the room's own block wins.
schedule.block_hint: No days selected means every day; an end before the start runs past midnight. Changes save right away.
devices.no_climate: No climate entities found in this area.
devices.no_temp_sensors: No temperature sensors found in this area.
devices.no_humidity_sensors: No humidity sensors found in this area.
devices.no_occupancy_sensors: No occupancy sensors found in this area
devices.occupancy_sensor_hint: Improves thermal model accuracy by tracking room occupancy
devices.occupancy_eco: Eco when the room is empty
devices.occupancy_eco_hint: When all occupancy sensors report the room empty for longer than the delay, the room drops to its eco temperature. As soon as someone is detected again, it follows its schedule. An empty room is kept at eco and only heats to comfort once someone is in it, so it takes a while to warm up. Temporary overrides, vacation mode and presence detection take priority.
devices.no_window_sensors: No window/door sensors found in this area.
devices.heating_system_type_info: After heating stops, radiators and especially underfloor systems continue to release stored heat. RoomMind accounts for this residual heat to avoid overshooting and improve model accuracy. Underfloor rooms also get longer minimum run times.
devices.underfloor_delay_hint: Underfloor heating has long restart times. A window-open delay of at least 5 minutes is recommended to avoid unnecessary shutoffs.
devices.heating_system_type_boost_hint: Tip: If the heating system has changed, you can accelerate re-learning under Settings.
devices.setback_auto_off: Turn off after an hour without demand
devices.setback_auto_off_hint: With an external temperature sensor and a trained model, the device is turned off after an hour without heating or cooling if RoomMind does not expect to need it in the next hour. Off by default: setback keeps the device on.
devices.idle_action_low_hint: Lowers the setpoint to the device minimum instead of sending off. Prevents TRVs that hibernate in off mode from losing later commands.
devices.setpoint_offset_hint: Use this if the device's own sensor reads differently from your room sensor. The offset is added to the room target before it is sent to the device (heating and cooling). Device reads colder than the room: negative value. Device reads warmer: positive value. Example: you want 24°, but while cooling the device thinks the room is 2° colder than it is and stops too early. Enter -2: the device then gets 22° and keeps running until the room is really at 24°. 0 = no offset.
devices.setpoint_mode_hint: Direct sends the actual room target to the device — best for thermostats and space heaters that regulate themselves. Proportional sends a boosted setpoint toward the device max_temp — best for radiator valves (TRVs).
devices.coil_dry_global_off_hint: Evaporator drying is switched off globally, so nothing runs for this device. Turn it on in the settings, or set this device to "Always on".
devices.valve_protection_exclude_hint: This entity will not be cycled by valve protection (e.g. virtual boiler entities)
devices.valve_closing_mode_hint: What the second value means. Most thermostats have a closing degree (SONOFF TRVZB: valve_closing_degree). The SONOFF TRV-ZBT has the valve opening while it does not heat instead (Zigbee2MQTT: idle_valve_position): pick "Opening while idle" there, or the valve stays open when the room needs no heat.
devices.valve_direct_control_hint: For thermostats that let Home Assistant set the valve opening (e.g. SONOFF TRVZB: valve_opening_degree and valve_closing_degree, both needed). RoomMind then holds the valve at the opening the room needs, e.g. 30 %, instead of opening it fully: fewer valve movements, quieter and more even heat. Clear the fields or switch off climate control and RoomMind hands the valve back to the thermostat's own control.
devices.valve_direct_control_toggle_hint: For thermostats that let Home Assistant set the valve opening (e.g. SONOFF TRVZB). RoomMind then holds the valve at the opening the room needs, e.g. 30 %, instead of opening it fully: fewer valve movements, quieter and more even heat. Switched off, or with climate control off, the valve goes back to the thermostat's own control.
devices.info.types_body: Thermostat means a radiator thermostat / TRV. Climate Device means an AC, heat pump, or other climate entity used for cooling or forced-air heating. Both are Home Assistant climate entities; the distinction is how RoomMind controls them.
devices.info.control_body: Setpoint mode only applies to thermostats in Full Control rooms with an external temperature sensor. Use Proportional when RoomMind should drive heating output by sending boosted setpoints. Use Direct when the device should regulate itself around the real target temperature.
devices.info.modes_body: When idle only applies to Climate Devices. Turn off powers the device down. Fan only keeps airflow without heating or cooling. Setback keeps the current mode active but moves the target 2°C away from the room target. This setback offset is currently fixed. Turn off after an hour without demand switches the device off when RoomMind does not expect to need it in the next hour (needs an external temperature sensor and a trained model). For Thermostats, Low keeps the TRV active at its minimum setpoint instead of off, useful for battery-powered Zigbee TRVs that sleep when set to off.
devices.info.heat_source_body: This appears only when a room has both a thermostat/TRV and a Climate Device plus an external temperature sensor. RoomMind can then choose which source should handle heating based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
covers.auto_control_hint: RoomMind closes blinds when solar gain is predicted to overheat the room.
covers.deploy_threshold_hint: Close blinds when predicted temperature exceeds target by this amount.
covers.min_position_hint: Blinds will never close further than this (0 = fully closed allowed).
covers.override_minutes_hint: How long to pause automatic control after manual cover movement. Set to 0 for no pause.
covers.no_covers_in_area: No cover entities found in this area.
covers.night_close_hint: Automatically close covers at sunset and open at sunrise.
covers.window_hold_hint: While a window or door sensor of this room is open, RoomMind does not lower the covers and catches up once it is closed. For blinds that would hit an open window (inside blinds, roof windows). RoomMind checks every 30 seconds and does not stop a cover that is already moving.
covers.schedule_section_hint: Define time windows for cover control using HA schedule helpers. In Force position mode the schedule's position overrides solar/thermal logic. In Allow solar protection mode RoomMind decides the position within the active window.
covers.schedule_position_hint: Cover position when this schedule is active (0% = fully closed, 100% = fully open).
covers.schedule_selector_hint: Choose which schedule is active. input_boolean: off=#1, on=#2. input_number: value selects schedule number.
covers.schedule_selector_warning: Multiple schedules configured but no selector set. Only the first schedule will be used.
covers.night_position_hint: Cover position when night close is active (0% = fully closed). Covers with an individual min. position will never go below that.
covers.night_close_elevation_hint: How far below or above the horizon the sun must be. 0° = exactly at sunset/sunrise. Negative = darker (e.g. -6° = dusk, when it's noticeably dark). Positive = still bright (e.g. 5° = sun still visible above horizon).
covers.night_close_offset_hint: Additional shift relative to the sun position threshold. Positive = close later (e.g. +20 = 20 min after threshold is reached), negative = close earlier.
covers.outdoor_min_temp_hint: Don't close covers for solar protection below this outdoor temperature. Solar heat gain is welcome when it's cold.
covers.per_cover_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces and optional individual minimum positions.
covers.per_cover_min_position_hint: Individual minimum position per cover. Covers will never close further than this. Useful when blinds are physically fully closed at a position > 0%.
covers.snap_deploy_hint: Close covers directly to the minimum position instead of gradually closing. Recommended for triple-pane windows where intermediate positions can cause thermal stress.
covers.info.selection_body: Select covers/blinds from this area or add entities from other areas. RoomMind tracks their position and can control them automatically.
covers.info.schedule_body: Use HA schedule helpers to define times when covers should close (e.g. privacy in the evening). The schedule's position attribute determines how far they close. Schedules override all other automatic logic.
covers.info.solar_body: When automatic control is enabled, RoomMind predicts whether solar radiation will overheat the room and closes blinds preventively. It uses learned thermal data when available, otherwise a conservative default. The deploy threshold controls how much predicted overshoot is needed before blinds close.
covers.info.night_body: Closes covers at sunset and opens them at sunrise. You can set a custom night position (e.g. 10% = almost closed but not fully).
covers.info.override_body: If you manually move a cover, RoomMind detects this and pauses automatic control for the configured duration. This prevents fighting with the user.
covers.info.priority_body: Manual override > Schedule > Night close > Solar/thermal control. Higher priority rules always win. When no rule applies, covers stay open.
covers.info.entities_body: RoomMind creates two entities per room for external use: switch.roommind_{area}_cover_auto (enable/disable automatic cover control — usable in automations or dashboards) and binary_sensor.roommind_{area}_cover_paused (on when manual override is active, e.g. after manually moving a cover).
covers.orientation_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces. RoomMind then shades only while the sun is actually on that side of the building. Without a direction, covers react to sunshine in general and may close from sunrise, even on a north window.
settings.climate_control_hint: When disabled, RoomMind continues to monitor all sensors and train the model, but sends no commands to your heating or cooling devices. Your devices keep their current mode and setpoint and may continue heating or cooling on their own. RoomMind will not turn them off.
settings.learning_hint: When paused, RoomMind stops collecting new measurement data and training the thermal model. Existing model data is preserved.
settings.smart_control_hint: Configure outdoor temperature limits for heating and cooling.
settings.outdoor_cooling_min_hint: AC stays off when outdoor temperature is below this value. A manual override ignores this limit
settings.outdoor_heating_max_hint: Heating stays off when outdoor temperature exceeds this value. A manual override ignores this limit
settings.control_mode_hint: Intelligent: MPC learns each room's thermal behavior and plans ahead (on/off control while it is still learning). Simple: on/off control with hysteresis only; the model keeps learning in the background but does not make decisions, and automatic blinds use a simpler solar estimate instead of the MPC forecast.
settings.comfort_weight_hint: Balances temperature precision against energy use. Comfort reacts earlier and stays closer to target. Efficiency allows more drift to reduce heating/cooling runtime. At the default and above, rooms are heated up ahead of a schedule block so they are warm when it starts; below the default it starts later, at full efficiency only shortly before the block.
settings.preheat_lead: Pre-heats up to {hours} h before a warmer schedule block.
settings.preheat_lead_none: No pre-heating: heats only shortly before a warmer schedule block.
settings.weather_entity_hint: Optional: enables predictive outdoor temperature planning, and acts as a fallback when the outdoor sensor is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify: Notify when outdoor temperature is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify_hint: Show a Home Assistant notification when neither the outdoor sensor nor the weather entity has reported a temperature for 30 minutes. While this is the case, RoomMind pauses thermal model learning to avoid corruption.
settings.prediction_enabled_hint: Show predicted temperature trend in analytics charts. Disable if you experience slow performance.
vacation.title: Vacation Mode
vacation.hint: Sets all rooms to a setback temperature until the end date.
analytics.info.accuracy_idle: How precisely the model predicts temperature when neither heating nor cooling is active. A lower value means the model understands your room's natural heat loss well. This is the first value to improve because idle data is collected continuously.
analytics.info.accuracy_heating: How precisely the model predicts temperature during active heating. This value stays high initially because the model needs real heating cycles to learn from. Once your heating has run a few times, this value will drop and MPC control becomes available.
analytics.info.confidence: Overall model readiness for intelligent MPC control, combining two factors: data quantity (how many idle and active-mode samples have been collected) and prediction accuracy (how precise the temperature forecasts are). Confidence starts at 0% and rises as the model collects data and learns. Around 50% means enough idle data but still waiting for heating/cooling cycles. Above 80% means the model has enough data and accurate predictions — MPC control becomes available. 100% is the theoretical maximum when predictions are as accurate as physically possible.
analytics.info.time_constant: How long it takes your room to naturally cool down halfway toward the outdoor temperature when heating is off. A longer time constant means better insulation — the room holds warmth longer. A short time constant means the room cools quickly. The model learns this by observing temperature drops during idle periods.
analytics.info.heating_rate: How strongly your heating affects the room temperature. A higher value means your heating system warms the room faster relative to its thermal mass. The model learns this by observing how quickly the temperature rises during active heating, and uses it to predict how long heating needs to run.
analytics.info.cooling_rate: How strongly your AC affects the room temperature. A higher value means the AC cools the room faster relative to its thermal mass. The model learns this by observing how quickly the temperature drops during active cooling, and uses it to predict how long the AC needs to run. The air near the sensor drops faster in the first minutes of a run and warms back up after it stops; the model tracks that part separately, so this value describes how fast the AC cools the whole room including walls and furniture.
analytics.info.solar_gain: How fast the sun warms the room at full sunshine (1000 W/m², a clear summer noon). Most of the time far less sun reaches the window: the line below shows what the sun adds right now (clouds and blinds included) and at most today under a clear sky. In winter that is often only a quarter of the full-sun value. Compare the heating strength with these two values. The model learns this by observing how the room warms during sunny periods when heating is off and uses it to reduce heating when sun is expected.
analytics.info.occupancy_gain: The estimated heat contribution from occupancy (people, pets, computers) while the room is occupied. The model learns this by observing temperature changes when the configured occupancy sensors are active. Separating this from solar gain prevents body heat from being misattributed to sunlight. Only shown when at least one occupancy sensor is configured for this room.
analytics.info.data_sources: Number of measurement samples used for model training.
analytics.info.data_points: Total number of observations the model has been trained on. More data points generally lead to better predictions. The model collects a new data point roughly every 3 minutes while RoomMind is running.
analytics.no_data: No data yet — model is learning
settings.intro.orphans: The Home Assistant area of these rooms was deleted. RoomMind no longer controls them but keeps their settings and what it learned: create the area again under its original name and the room continues where it left off. Delete a room here if you no longer need it.
settings.orphans_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" with its settings and learned data?
settings.reset_hint: Clear learned thermal model data and history. The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_all_hint: Clear thermal data and history for all rooms at once.
settings.reset_all_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for ALL rooms? All models will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_room_hint: Select a room to clear its thermal data and history.
settings.reset_room_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for this room? The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.boost_hint: The thermal model learns your room's heating and cooling behavior over time. After major changes (new radiator, AC, insulation, furniture), the model may be inaccurate. This increases the model's uncertainty so it adapts faster to new conditions.
analytics.chart_info_body:
**Lines:** The solid orange line shows the measured room temperature. The green dashed line is the target temperature from your schedule. The blue dotted line is the model's temperature prediction.

**Shaded areas:** Red shading marks heating periods, blue marks cooling, and teal marks times when a window was open.

**Future forecast (right of the 'now' line):** The green dashed line shows the upcoming schedule targets for the next 3 hours. The blue dotted line shows the predicted temperature trend.

**Prediction modes:** When 'MPC active' is shown, the prediction uses the full MPC optimizer with intelligent pre-heating/pre-cooling. While the model is still learning, a simpler simulation is used.

**Limitations:** The prediction assumes current conditions stay constant (outdoor temperature, window state). The simulation accuracy depends on how well the thermal model has learned your room — early on, predictions may be less accurate. Once MPC activates, predictions become significantly more reliable.
presence.title: Presence Detection
presence.hint: Uses eco temperature when nobody is home.
presence.hint_detail: When enabled, all rooms switch to eco temperature as soon as none of the configured persons are home. You can optionally restrict per room which persons are relevant.
presence.room_help_body: Select which persons are relevant for this room. The room switches to eco temperature when none of the selected persons are home. Without selection, the global rule applies: eco when nobody is home.
presence.room_none_assigned: Global rule — eco when nobody is home
presence.missing_entity_hint: This entity no longer exists in Home Assistant — uncheck it to remove it from this room.
presence.ignore_hint: Controls how this room reacts to presence. You can assign specific persons below. The room switches to eco when none of the assigned persons are home. Use the toggle above to skip detection entirely and always follow the schedule.
presence.help_ignore_body: When enabled, this room skips presence detection entirely. It always follows its schedule and never switches to eco based on who is home. Useful for rooms that should maintain temperature regardless of presence, such as a server room, a pet room, or a guest room used by someone not tracked by Home Assistant.
presence.tile_ignored: Presence detection is ignored. Room always follows its schedule.
presence.clears_override_hint: When nobody is home, manual overrides are paused and the room follows the away action. When someone returns, the override resumes until it expires.
valve_protection.title: Valve Protection
valve_protection.hint: Periodically opens idle TRV valves briefly to prevent seizing or calcification.
valve_protection.interval_hint: How long a valve can be idle before being cycled (1–90 days)
compressor.title: Compressor Protection
compressor.members_hint: Select all climate devices powered by this compressor (indoor splits, TRVs on radiators, fan coils).
compressor.min_run_hint: Compressor must run at least this long once started.
compressor.min_off_hint: Compressor must stay off at least this long after stopping.
compressor.master_entity_hint: The central unit that powers the indoor devices in this group, e.g. a gas boiler, outdoor heat pump unit, or ducted AC master switch. RoomMind will turn it on when any room needs heating or cooling, and off when all rooms are idle. Leave empty to use only the action script or short-cycle protection.
compressor.conflict_resolution_hint: Determines what happens when some rooms need heating while others need cooling at the same time. Heating priority: heating always wins (safest for frost protection). Cooling priority: cooling always wins. Majority: the mode with more rooms wins, ties go to heating. Outdoor temperature: uses the outdoor heating max threshold from settings to decide automatically.
compressor.action_script_hint: A Home Assistant script that runs whenever the heating/cooling demand changes. Useful for systems that need special commands, e.g. cancelling a Vaillant Quick Veto or toggling a relay. Works with or without a master device. Without a master device, only the script is triggered. Receives variables: action (heat/cool/idle), master_entity, members, active_members.
compressor.enforce_uniform_mode_hint: All thermostats in this group must operate in the same HVAC mode (all heating or all cooling). Rooms that disagree with the resolved group mode will be set to idle. Use this for heat pumps that start automatically but require all connected units to run the same mode.
coil_dry.title: Evaporator drying
coil_dry.hint: After cooling, keep the indoor fan running for a while before the AC really switches off. Dries the evaporator so no biofilm forms and the next start does not smell musty.
coil_dry.duration_hint: How long the fan keeps running (1–60 min). At a low fan speed allow roughly twice as long as at a high one.
coil_dry.min_cooling_hint: Only dry after the AC has cooled for at least this long. Short cooling bursts are added up (1–240 min).
coil_dry.mode_dry_warning: In dry mode the compressor keeps running and cools the coil down again, which works against drying. Only pick this if your unit's dry mode is fan-driven.
coil_dry.fan_mode_hint: A higher speed dries faster but is louder. Speeds the device does not report are skipped — it then keeps its current one.
coil_dry.drain_hint: Leave the AC off first so condensate can drain, then start the fan (0–15 min). Reduces how much moisture is blown back into the room.
mold.title: Mold Risk Protection
mold.detection_desc: Receive notifications when humidity indicates mold risk
mold.threshold_hint: Alert when room humidity stays above this value
mold.insulation_hint: Used to estimate how cold the coldest spot of your exterior walls gets (corners, window reveals). If unsure, keep Standard. Needs an outdoor temperature.
mold.sustained_hint: Alert only after risk persists for this long
mold.prevention_desc: Automatically raise temperature to reduce mold risk
mold.intensity_hint: Warmer air reduces surface humidity on cold walls. Light is usually sufficient for moderate risk, Strong can lower surface humidity by up to 8–10% — but uses noticeably more energy.
settings.intro.sensors: Configure outdoor sensors and weather data for accurate climate control.
settings.intro.control: Choose how RoomMind controls your climate devices and set priority and thresholds.
settings.intro.presence: Automatically reduce temperature when nobody is home.
settings.intro.vacation: Set all rooms to a reduced temperature while you are away.
settings.intro.valve: Periodically move idle TRV valves to prevent seizing or calcification.
settings.intro.compressor: Manage groups of indoor units that share an outdoor compressor or central heating source. Optionally assign a master device (boiler, outdoor unit) to automatically turn on/off based on room demand. Short-cycle protection prevents rapid on/off switching that can damage equipment.
settings.intro.mold: Monitor humidity and automatically reduce mold risk.
settings.intro.notifications: Configure who receives alerts and how.
settings.intro.learning: Manage thermal model training and accelerate re-learning after changes.
settings.intro.reset: Clear learned thermal model data. The model will start learning from scratch.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.enabled_hint: When disabled, no notifications are sent — neither to devices nor to the HA sidebar.
notifications.desc: Choose which devices receive alerts. Without targets, alerts appear in the HA sidebar.
notifications.add_target_hint: Type the entity ID if your device is not listed (e.g. notify.mobile_app_...). You can find it under Settings → Devices → your phone → Notify entity.
notifications.cooldown_hint: Minimum time between repeated alerts per room
notifications.mold_prevention_notify_hin: Also send a notification when prevention activates (temperature raised)
heat_source.toggle_hint: When this room has both radiator thermostats and an AC/heat pump, RoomMind intelligently routes heating demand to the most efficient device based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
heat_source.primary_delta_hint: Only activate the primary source when the temperature gap exceeds this value. Below this threshold, only the fast secondary source is used.
heat_source.outdoor_threshold_hint: Above this outdoor temperature, prefer the AC/heat pump (higher efficiency). Below, prefer the gas boiler/radiator.
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor: Min. outdoor temp for AC heating
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor_hint: Disable AC heating entirely below this temperature to protect the heat pump hardware.
devices.valve_closing_entity_hint: Keeps the valve at the set opening whatever the thermostat's own control wants. Filled in automatically when the device names it like the opening degree (valve_closing_degree).
tou.title: Time-of-Use control
tou.enabled_hint: Shape room targets by tariff tier and pre-condition in cheap windows.
tou.source_hint: RoomMind reads whatever you bind here. Pick one source for the current tier and one for planning ahead — anything bound but not selected is kept, just ignored.
tou.src.rate_desc: Pick this when you have a numeric price but no period text (Tibber, Nord Pool, spot rates, or a price you maintain yourself). Cost thresholds below decide which price counts as peak, mid or ultra-low.
tou.src.period_desc: Pick this when an integration names the active tariff period for you (e.g. Hydro One's active-peak sensor). Words like on-peak, mid-peak, off-peak and overnight are recognized automatically.
tou.src.flags_desc: Fallback for automations that toggle one boolean per tariff period. Tells RoomMind what is active now — nothing about what comes next.
tou.lk.calendar_desc: Recommended. Bind a calendar per tier and RoomMind sees the entire tariff timeline: pre-conditioning fills the room before a peak, coast rules carry it through, exactly at the event boundaries. Works with the built-in Local Calendar — no automations required.
tou.lk.next_rate_desc: Pick this when your provider publishes the price of the period that starts at the next change (a "next rate" sensor). RoomMind classifies that rate with the cost thresholds below to learn which tier is coming; the change time still comes from the next-change timestamp.
tou.lk.next_change_desc: For integrations that only say when the next change starts (e.g. Hydro One's "next peak starts"). RoomMind sees one boundary ahead: it plans to stop or start conditioning there, but nothing beyond. Bind the sensor and pick the tier the change leads into.
tou.lk.none_desc: Shaping only: targets ease while an expensive tier is active and rise during cheap ones, but nothing is pre-conditioned or coasted, because RoomMind can't see the boundaries ahead.
tou.next_change_tier_hint: Which tier the change leads into — the sensor only gives the time. For a "next peak starts" sensor pick Peak. "Not set" disables the lookahead.
tou.next_rate_hint: The rate is mapped to a tier by the cost thresholds, like the cost-sensor source. When the next-period price cannot be placed without thresholds, bind the next-period name sensor below instead. Using an intermediary helper or calendar with custom rules can reduce exposure to provider failures.
tou.next_period_hint: For providers that publish the name of the period that follows (e.g. Hydro One's "next peak": "ulo_mid_peak"). RoomMind reads it with the same wording recognition as the current period, so it learns the coming tier without cost thresholds. Leave empty if your provider has no such sensor.
tou.dic_next_hint_no_tier: The future view is bound but nothing says which tier comes next — pick the tier, or bind the next-period name sensor.
tou.dic_next_hint_no_time: The next-change sensor gave no timestamp (it answered a period name). The coming tier and price show without the time — bind the provider's "next change starts" sensor for the clock.
tou.dic_next_hint_no_price: The next tier is known but no next-period price is available yet; RoomMind will fall back to its last known value for that tier.
tou.dic_title: Tiers as your source feeds them
tou.dic_hint: Confirm RoomMind reads the tariff you expect: prices are pulled live from your bound sources whenever you open this view; when a cost source is down the last valid price is kept (marked last known).
tou.dic_not_running: Waiting for the first update cycle to read your tariff sources.
tou.dic_remove_alias: Assigned by you — click to remove
tou.dic_unmapped_hint: Assign each period name to its tier; the mapping applies from the next update on.
tou.dic_cutoff_hint: ≥ marks a configured cost threshold, not a price; (last known) marks the persisted value used while a cost source is unavailable.
tou.fine_tune_hint: The defaults suit typical TOU tariffs. Open to adjust the store limits and price weighting.
tou.rate_aux_hint: Optional here: feeds the energy rate sensors and price-weighted planning; the tier still comes from the selected source.
tou.sources_hint: Add sensor-driven periods the grid tariff cannot describe — a generator burning gas, solar production, grid-export credit. Each carries its own price and behaves like a tariff period: it overrides the grid tier while its sensor holds, and rules can anchor on its start and end. Listed order = priority. The grid tariff keeps being tracked underneath.
tou.sources_cost_hint: Prices are per kWh in your unit (0 for self-consumed solar, negative for export credit; blank leaves the tier unpriced and economically neutral). A price below the cheapest grid tier invites pre-conditioning; above it invites load-shifting away.
tou.source_kind.numeric_below: Value is below (negative grid value = export)
tou.calendars_hint: Calendar events mark tier windows; the MPC plans coasting across them.
tou.rate_windows_hint: An alternative to calendar entities: each row applies its rate between two times on the selected days (no day ticked = every day; an end before the start runs past midnight). Rates map to tiers with the same cost thresholds.
tou.flags_hint: Automations that toggle one boolean per tariff period.
tou.shaping_hint: The band no target may leave, the largest swing the store layer may take around the schedule, and the price ratio that must justify even trying. Rooms can adjust these on their card.
tou.price_weighting_hint: The MPC charges rooms in cheap blocks and stops at tier changes, coasting through expensive ones on stored heat.
tou.thresholds_hint: Only needed when no period sensor/flags are bound. Rates at/above each value classify as that tier; rates at/below the ultra-low value classify as ultra-low.
tou.room_off_summary: Not tariff-aware — enable storing or the tariff schedule below.
tou.store_hint: Pre-heats before expensive periods and coasts through them on stored heat — cheaper overall, in exchange for a wider temperature swing. The room never leaves your allowed targets and stores only when the price gap justifies it; manual overrides, vacation and arrive-rule promises keep priority.
tou.schedule_only_summary: Tariff rules only — no automatic storing
tou.limits_note: Swing up to {swing} °C around the schedule; targets stay inside {hmin}–{hmax} °C heating and {cmin}–{cmax} °C cooling; storing starts when a period costs at least ×{gap} of the cheaper window before it.
tou.room_limits_hint: Blank fields inherit the global limits (Settings → Time-of-Use).
tou.arrive_model_note: The temperature the room must have at the period change is derived from the learned room model, so the room coasts to the target exactly at the arrival time. Until the model is confident, the row holds the flat target.
tou.card_schedule_hint: Scheduling lives on the device cards: pick a tariff period there and RoomMind anchors the action to its boundaries.
tou.override_between_hint: Optional: only fire when the change itself happens inside this time range.
tou.override_days_hint: Only rows whose tier change falls on a ticked day fire. Nothing ticked = every day.
tou.override_name_hint: Pick an existing name to switch this row to that shared rule; type a new one to rename (a fresh name forks a copy for this room).
tou.override_sides_hint: Each side can steer a fixed temperature or aim at the room's own Comfort or Eco target. Leave a side blank to skip this row in that mode — a heating-only row never touches cooling.
tou.schedule_hint: Temporary target overrides anchored on a tariff period instead of the clock. The normal schedule and all other rules keep controlling heating and cooling — a row only bends the target while it holds.
tou.pick_rule_hint: Copying reuses an existing shared rule (an edit propagates to every room using it); a new rule belongs to this room until another references it.
tou.rename_hint: Renaming forks a copy for this room — unless the name matches an existing rule, then both become one shared rule.
tou.row_priority_note: When two rules steer the same side and their windows overlap, the lowest rule wins — drag the handle or use the arrows to reorder.
tou.window_next: Controls {side}: next window {start} → {end} ({dur}) · fires {count}× in view
tou.window_none: No tariff change ahead matches this anchor — check the period, weekdays and time filters.
tou.save_stage_hint: Changes are staged — they apply when you collapse this row.
tou.discard_new_rule: This rule has no name yet — rules need one. Discard it?
tou.discard_unnamed: This rule has no name — rules need one. Discard the changes to it?
tou.rule_missing: This row's rule no longer exists — remove the row or add the rule again.
tou.rule_used_in: Used in {count} rooms — changes apply to all of them.
tou.schedule_empty: No rows yet. Add one below.
tou.schedule_enabled_label: Enable tariff schedule for this room
tou.schedule_off_hint: The tariff schedule is switched off for this room — its rules stay saved, they just do not act.
settings.intro.tou: Link an electricity tariff source and shape room targets by time of use. Rooms keep comfort where energy is cheap and coast on stored heat where it is expensive. This feature can also be used with helpers or a calendar for other edge cases such as with a local microgrid that uses different fuels to generate power, or to store excess solar generation as thermal mass.
